stages.title: v0.1–v0.3 — Deterministic core & reproducible environment
stages.desc: The simulate-with-models / narrate-with-LLMs core, the knowledge graph, and the environment moving from assumed to stamped and checked.

tasks.title: v0.1 — simulation-driven design review
tasks.aufgabe: Establish the deterministic core (rng, events, ledger, versioning) and the first evidence bundle.
tasks.ziel: A seeded, replayable simulation core with zero LLM calls on the decision path.
tasks.stand: Released 2026-08-02. Bundle archived at evidence/v0.1/20260802T150651+0000 and kept untouched as the comparison baseline.

decisions.text: Architectural rule fixed: the deterministic core decides what happens, the narration layer only verbalises it and never makes a decision.

tasks.title: Knowledge graph + GraphRAG retrieval (build order 2 & 3)
tasks.aufgabe: Load Hetionet via kg_loader, wire graph/client.py, and build the NL->Cypher retriever with allowlist validation.
tasks.ziel: The persona grounds on retrieved subgraph facts with citations instead of drifting.
tasks.stand: Done. Persona-relevant metaedge slice loads 47,031 nodes / 277,997 edges, idempotent on re-run. graph/schema.py is the single source of truth for labels, rel types and metaedge codes.

achievements.text: cypher_guard validates LLM-written Cypher before execution.

decisions.text: Hetionet has only 137 diseases; heart failure is deliberately NOT aliased to a near neighbour — resolve() returns None and the persona grounds on nothing. Grounding on the wrong disease is worse than grounding on none.

tasks.title: Cohort generator + protocol stress-test surface (build order 4 & 5)
tasks.aufgabe: Sample N personas across a subpopulation with copula-coupled trait axes; expose real eligibility evaluation and per-patient burden reporting via the API.
tasks.ziel: Cohort generation and scenario stress-testing usable end to end, offline.
tasks.stand: Done. Build-order items 2–5 are all closed; only ingest/synthea_loader.py remains open.

tasks.title: v0.3 — the environment release
tasks.aufgabe: Declare dependencies in pyproject, resolve with uv.lock, render requirements.txt, enforce sync in CI, close the float-accumulation class, and stamp the environment into every artifact.
tasks.ziel: Every guarantee holds outside the author's machine — environment stamped and checked, not assumed.
tasks.stand: Released 2026-08-14. 859 Python tests across 3.11/3.12/3.13, 27 SPA tests, 3 E2E specs, all green per push.

achievements.text: Four bugs (networkx undeclared, dash venv sourcing, Neumaier sum drift, venv drift) closed as one construction rather than four patches.
CI matrix: Python on 3.11/3.12/3.13, Node once, full leg on the oldest.

validations.text: Guard fires: tests/test_float_accumulation.py walks the core AST and fails on any bare sum() whose operands are not stated. 8 of 10 int-sum markers verify against a schema; the 2 that cannot (Neo4j driver rows) are enumerated by the test rather than remembered.

decisions.text: Environment enforcement in tiers: refuse on lock-hash mismatch, warn on interpreter difference inside the supported range, refuse outside it. The warn tier is only honest while the matrix keeps running goldens on every interpreter.

tasks.title: Prompt v2 re-record
tasks.aufgabe: Re-record the narration battery with exactly one declared variable changed — the prompt — against the same weights, sampling and pre-registered bars.
tasks.ziel: Kill the doubled-citation defect at source rather than in the renderer, and close the model_recall margin.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-14 (commit 168a686). A second measurement, not a repair; v0.1's bundle stays untouched as the comparison baseline.

achievements.text: Double-citation dead at source: 0 of 30 raw responses contain an inline [F###] marker (v1: 7 of 25). Renderer stripping stays as defence in depth and now has nothing to strip.
Bundles archive both layers — segments as the model emitted them, plus the rendered text. Dead-and-wrong take-fetching code replaced.

validations.text: model_recall 0.525 against the 0.5 bar on the full battery, up from v1's exactly-on-the-bar 0.500 — two independent readings above the bar.
Friction hypothesis supported but CONFOUNDED: quarantine 5/30 -> 0/30, retries 6.7% -> 0%, but some of that is attributable to a separate finding and the two causes are not yet separated.

stages.title: v0.4 — State-citation (P/B/J/E namespaces)
stages.desc: The active workstream. v2's factual_fraction collapse on burden and mitigation is claimed to be a state-citation gap; the pre-registered shape says what would falsify that.

tasks.title: Pre-register the v3 expected shape + control arm
tasks.aufgabe: Write the expected v3 shape and its falsifier BEFORE the namespaces are built and before any v3 recording.
tasks.ziel: A prediction that is a prediction — committed before the numbers exist, same rule as pass_bars.json.
tasks.stand: Done (1e0ce63), amended to four namespaces (c98cb19). Amendment legitimate only because nothing is recorded yet, and stated rather than slipped in.

decisions.text: The escape clause is a CONTROL ARM, not a ceiling number. Graph-knowledge tags (ae, tx, proc) gained nothing from P/B/E and must stay flat within 0.10. sym is explicitly NOT a control — symptoms are simulated state, so P-citations there are legitimate.

Four namespaces, not three: P- profile, B- derived barriers, J- journey milestones, E- RESERVED for simulation event-log entries. An id namespace whose meaning changes later makes every v3 recording silently ambiguous.

tasks.title: Build the P/B/J/E id namespaces
tasks.aufgabe: Implement the four state-citation namespaces under constrained decoding: P- profile, B- derived barriers, J- journey milestones, E- reserved and empty for unsimulated personas.
tasks.ziel: The persona can cite its own declared state, not only graph knowledge.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-23. narration/state_facts.py derives P/B/J from the persona; E- is declared and pinned empty by tests/test_state_citation.py. PROMPT_VERSION 3 (cassettes invalidated on purpose), the ids in the decode enum, click-through dispatching on namespace, and the strip_state_ids canary lever wired so state_coverage can fail. H is unblocked.

achievements.text: Four namespaces live: P- profile (a declared surface, PROFILE_FIELDS), B- derived barriers (the id IS the barrier name, so the graph join survives), J- journey milestones, E- reserved and empty.
state_coverage implemented with a kind-independent denominator, plus the strip_state_ids canary lever. run_canary refuses `sensitive` unless BOTH the grounding lever and the state lever fire.
Citation click-through closes the loop from the state side: a B- id expands to the derived barrier and the profile field the simulation computed it from.

validations.text: Canary proves the new axis can fail: state_coverage collapses under strip_state_ids while model_recall holds (state_lever_clean). An unexercised axis is reported as its own verdict, not as a dead lever.
Context check: worst battery prompt ~2230 tokens against num_ctx 8192 with 700 reserved. The larger prompt does not put H at risk of silent head truncation.
896 offline tests green, including 23 new in tests/test_state_citation.py.

decisions.text: E- emits nothing and derive_state_facts takes no PersonaState. A persona with a state slice therefore has prose about missed visits but no id for it — the coverage finding the pre-registration already recorded, left as a finding rather than repaired by widening J-.

The state surface is offered WHOLE, not ranked against the question. A relevance scorer for state would be a second unevaluated variable inside a run whose entire design is one — the same reason fact-order permutation stays off for v3. If v3 shows volume-driven citation, the ranker gets its own paired comparison.

FINDING for H's reading: state ids are now 64% of the enum (mean 28 state against 16 graph per battery case). A rise in state citation could be volume-driven, so f_recall_holds_independently and state_citation_share are the arms that separate that from recovery.

v3_expected_shape.json amended before any recording: state_coverage gained an explicit denominator, and the P/B/E shorthand left over from the three-namespace draft now reads P/B/J. A denominator chosen after seeing results would not be a pre-registration.

tasks.title: Record the v3 battery against the pre-registered bars
tasks.aufgabe: Run the battery with the namespaces live, changing exactly one declared variable, and write the bundle beside v0.1 and v0.3.
tasks.ziel: A third reading comparable to the first two.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-23. Battery recorded against qwen2.5:7b-instruct@845dbda0ea48, prompt v3: 30/30 takes accepted, 0 quarantined, canary sensitive on both levers, all 8 pre-registered pass bars met. Bundle at evidence/v0.4/20260823T170152+0000. Caveat recorded in its NOTE.md: the aggregates are not reproducible from the committed cassette (see task N).

achievements.text: Battery re-authored: expect_facts (retrieval's own top ranks) replaced by authored must/may sets with alternation groups. Every inherited id reviewed against the persona it names.
Three pre-registered arms had no metric and now do: feeling_floor, inline_marker_takes and f_recall_holds_independently.
scripts/state_dumps.py regenerates the authoring worksheet from inputs only — it reads no cassette, by design.

v3 battery recorded: 30/30 accepted, 0 quarantined, hard_failure_rate 0.0, citation_validity 1.0. Canary fired on both levers — strip_instructions takes model_recall 0.586 -> 0.052, strip_state_ids takes state_coverage 0.564 -> 0.0.

validations.text: Expectation contract tests generated from battery contents: every expected id must exist in the graph or be derivable for that persona; must-sets stay 1-3 groups; both the F arm and the state axis have enough cases to grade.
f_recall semantics pinned by two stubs: satisfying a mixed alternation through the profile clears model_recall and misses f_recall, which is the arm working rather than a bug.

Reading protocol followed in its committed order: canary, then the five seed-chosen takes read in full, then quarantine (empty), then aggregates. The takes are terse but not degenerate; the sym take is pure feeling and uncited, which is the question doing its job rather than a miss.

decisions.text: COVERAGE FINDING: copd-s42-0005 has no derived barriers, so every mitigation fact retrieval offers is about a barrier it does not have. Its must-set is its own circumstances — a question with no correct answer before these ids existed.

Several inherited F-expectations contradicted their persona (a persona with a car expected to cite "no reliable way to get to the site"; a persona on metformin expected to cite insulin glargine). Dropped, not inherited.
Recall is NOT comparable to v0.1/v0.3 under re-authored expectations, and the battery says so in its own description. f_recall carries the pre-registered floor for graph recall instead.

tasks.title: Adjudicate: recovery or over-correction?
tasks.aufgabe: Check burden and mitigation factual_fraction against the controls. If burden and mitigation recover while ae/tx/proc hold flat within 0.10, the new ids did the work. If everything rises together it is over-correction, however good the burden numbers look.
tasks.ziel: A verdict the pre-registration can actually adjudicate, not a number chosen after the fact.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-24. Verdict: RECOVERY WITHOUT STATE CITATION — burden 0.400->0.700 and mitigation 0.443->0.933 with ae/tx/proc flat, but state_coverage 0.564 under its 0.6 floor. 12 of 13 arms passed. Written to the bundle as adjudication.json by scripts/adjudicate_bundle.py.

achievements.text: adjudication.py reads the arms from v3_expected_shape.json, transcribes no threshold, and carries the amendment trail into the verdict.

adjudicate_bundle() reads an archived bundle and leaves the verdict in it; the bundle README gains it as step 5, read LAST so it cannot colour the reading of the raw takes. Reproducible from the archived files without a model run.

validations.text: Every branch of the reading tree is reachable against a synthesised report (tests/test_adjudication.py) — the TestGateCanActuallyFail move. The branch that matters is OVER-CORRECTION: burden excellent while the controls rose with it.

The branch's stated cause does NOT match this run, and that is the finding. Relabelling would be circumstantial claims marked `feeling` with no ids; 17 of the 18 uncovered segments are marked `factual` and carry graph citations. The canary corroborates from the other side: under strip_state_ids f_recall RISES 0.531 -> 0.694. The two id families compete for citation slots — a budgeting habit, not an evasion.

decisions.text: A tag below its floor outranks another above its ceiling: a tag that did not recover falsifies the diagnosis whatever a second tag did.
Recovery with state_coverage under its floor is NOT recovery — that is relabelling, the over-correction signature in its purest form.
Caveats travel with the numbers rather than being remembered: recall comparability, the 64% enum asymmetry, a thin circumstantial denominator, and degeneracy sending the reader to the raw takes.

The shape file is NOT amended to fit. A fused segment citing both id families is the next prompt iteration, and it is a separate explicit commit — never made in the same breath as reporting a result against the file it would edit.

tasks.title: Close two instrument defects found while adjudicating
tasks.aufgabe: Make the report and the cassette describe one generation, and make context_overflow_rate a bar that can actually fail.
tasks.ziel: Evidence that reproduces from its own artifacts, and no pre-registered bar that passes by construction.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-24. Both fixed and pinned by tests. The v0.4 bundle is annotated rather than retro-fixed — it records what happened.

achievements.text: score() gained on_take, so one generation feeds both the report and the cassette. A live run now costs half the model calls, which also halves exposure to the adapter timeout that cost a recording on 2026-08-23.

context_overflow_rate is computed from cases the guard refused, over cases ATTEMPTED rather than scored, and an overflowed case leaves every behavioural denominator instead of scoring as a grounding failure.

validations.text: TestScoringAndRecordingSeeTheSameSample: one call per case, the handed-over take renders to what was scored, and a retried case hands over the REPAIRED take — the recorder used to archive first attempts while the report scored retried ones.
TestOverflowIsMeasuredNotAssumed runs a battery whose every prompt overflows and requires the hard bar to FAIL. Same move as TestGateCanActuallyFail.

decisions.text: MEASURED: two of thirty v0.4 takes drifted between the scoring pass and the recording pass, moving state_coverage from 0.5641 to 0.5135. Both readings miss the 0.6 floor, so the adjudication branch is unchanged — but the headline figure is not precise to three digits and the bundle now says so.
Every bundle before 2026-08-24 shows context_overflow_rate observed 0.0 PASSED. Read that as UNEVALUATED, not as evidence no prompt overflowed.
The v0.4 bundle is annotated, not corrected. A bundle is the record of what happened; rewriting its numbers would make it a record of what we wish had.

tasks.title: Read the uncovered circumstantial segments
tasks.aufgabe: state_coverage missed its floor and the adjudication branch named the cause as relabelling. That phrase was never measured. Read all 18 uncovered segments over the committed cassette, offline.
tasks.ziel: Know what the uncovered segments actually are, so the next pre-registration fixes the right thing.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-25. 18 of 37 circumstantial segments carry no state id. 17 of the 18 cite graph facts and are valid; 1 is relabelling. The verdict stands; the mechanism named in it does not.
achievements: Pure read over tests/cassettes/narration_battery.json — 30 takes, no model run, no network. Replay gives state_coverage 0.5135 over 37 circumstantial segments.
Of the 18 uncovered: 17 cite graph facts only and are kind `factual`; 1 cites nothing and is kind `feeling`; 0 lacked an offered state id. Not one is an uncited factual claim.
docs/okf/concepts/state-coverage-denominator.md records the read, and v3-reading.md now says the branch label's stated cause did not hold.
validations: Human read of all 18 segment texts: ~9 are denominator false positives (clinical claims in the first person, correctly citing graph facts), ~8 are compound segments citing their mitigation half and not the circumstance riding along with it, 1 is relabelling.
0 of 18 had no state id available, so no miss is explained by 'never had one to cite'.
decisions: The pre-registered shape file is NOT edited. The floor was missed on both readings, the branch is unchanged, and an expectation revised after seeing results is not an expectation. The denominator fix belongs in the next pre-registration.

is_circumstantial cannot separate a first-person CLINICAL claim from a first-person CIRCUMSTANTIAL one, and that gap is most of this miss. Its bias toward including is deliberate and sound; the instrument, not the bias, is what needs the change.

stages.title: Grounding in real data
stages.desc: Retire the literature ballparks. The last open build-order item is the gate for everything in this stage.

tasks.title: ingest/synthea_loader.py — real Synthea CSV joins -> PatientDNA
tasks.aufgabe: Join real Synthea CSV exports into the PatientDNA schema. Search TODO(claude-code) markers for the exact insertion points.
tasks.ziel: Persona generation draws on real distributions instead of condition-based priors alone.
tasks.stand: The one open build-order item (items 2–5 are done).

tasks.title: Re-derive epidemiology priors from loaded data
tasks.aufgabe: Replace cohort/epidemiology.py literature ballparks with priors derived from ingested data, and lift the do-not-quote caveat once they are sourced.
tasks.ziel: A number from cohort/epidemiology.py can be quoted as a finding.
tasks.stand: Blocked on synthea_loader. Until then: never quote a number from that module as a finding.

stages.title: Identifiability & product surface
stages.desc: Close the one knowingly unidentifiable parameter, then widen the surface from demo to usable tool.

tasks.title: Third anchor for cumulative_burden_weight
tasks.aufgabe: Design an anchor that varies per-visit burden at a fixed visit count, so cumulative_burden_weight separates from burden_increment_weight.
tasks.ziel: The parameter is estimated rather than frozen at zero.
tasks.stand: Ships frozen at zero — unidentifiable from two anchors. Known and declared, not hidden.

tasks.title: Scenario comparison views + exportable reports
tasks.aufgabe: Add scenario comparison output and exportable reports on top of Scenario Lab, Interview Room and Cohort Studio.
tasks.ziel: A stakeholder can run a comparison and take an artifact away without the author present.

tasks.title: Boundary tests for the three uncovered narration endpoints
tasks.aufgabe: Cover /persona/narrate, /panel/run and /persona/interview at the HTTP boundary. The narration internals are tested hard — prompt goldens, the citation gate, cassettes, memory semantics under permutation — but all three endpoints in front of them had no test touching them at all.
tasks.ziel: Every production endpoint is exercised at its boundary, and each new assertion is shown to fail when the behaviour it names is broken.
tasks.stand: Done 2026-08-25. tests/test_narration_api.py, 11 tests; suite 935 -> 946. Endpoint coverage 15/18 -> 18/18. Every assertion was mutation-checked and one was rewritten after the check proved it vacuous.
achievements: tests/test_narration_api.py — 11 boundary tests over /persona/narrate, /panel/run and /persona/interview: cited-skeleton shape offline, the check/grounded split, out-of-range persona_index, panel size bounds, mechanical theme attribution, offline determinism, and PatientDNA validation.
Endpoint coverage is now 18 of 18; it was 15 of 18, and the three missing were exactly the narration surface — the one nondeterministic layer in the system.
validations: Mutation canary, 7 of 7 caught: leaking the checker internals, 404 instead of 400 on a bad persona_index, accepting a one-person panel, hard-wiring ungrounded_statements to 0, attributing a theme to a persona who never spoke, dropping the disclaimer, and claiming an offline reply was model-written.
decisions: test_panel_ungrounded_count was rewritten after the mutation canary proved it VACUOUS: offline every statement grounds, so recomputing the count from the returned statements compares 0 to 0 and passes against an endpoint hard-wired to report 0. It now monkeypatches run_panel to return a transcript that actually contains an ungrounded statement. Same species as a pass bar supplied as a literal — an assertion that cannot discriminate is not coverage.
Linked to KR2.1 rather than to a new KR: this is suite-integrity work, so it widens what 'the suite' covers without moving a grade that was already met.

tasks.title: is_circumstantial v2 — instrument correction, blind validation pending
tasks.aufgabe: Define the state_coverage denominator from namespace semantics instead of first-person grammar, validate it blind, then rescore v3 under both instruments and publish the pair.
tasks.ziel: An instrument correction that is visibly an instrument correction, never folded into a model comparison.
tasks.stand: Blind labels in, both instruments scored. v2 beats v1 on agreement (0.6923 vs 0.6154) and kappa (0.3113 vs -0.0484), so the pre-registered comparative criterion adopts it. Blocked on one decision: the floor value under v2 semantics.
achievements: src/spp/narration/circumstantial.py — first person AND at least one term the persona's P/B/J facts carry that no offered graph fact does. Derived from PROFILE_FIELDS and the offered-fact contract, not from the segments.
Rescored the committed v3 cassette, zero model calls: v1 0.5135 (19/37), v2 0.6000 (18/30). The 15 dropped segments are the clinical-claim class; the true relabelling case survives under both.
tests/test_circumstantial_v2.py — 5 tests, including TestNotWiredIn asserting evaluation.py does not import v2.
Blind labels from an independent rater, text only: 38 y!, 6 y?, 8 n, 1 abstention. Committed as tests/eval/instrument_v2_labels.json.

v1 kappa is BELOW CHANCE (-0.0484) on this labelled set. On coverable segments the two instruments tie on raw agreement (0.6957 each) and split on kappa 0.0359 vs 0.3347 — raw agreement alone would have decided it wrong.
All 15 of v2's misses cluster into three named classes with none left over: own regimen (8), shared circumstance term (5), uncoverable y? (2).
validations: NOT validated against labels. The number is an instrument correction under review and is reported beside v1's, never instead of it.

state_coverage against the label-validated denominator: 0.5263 (20/38), schema_gap_rate 0.1364 (6/44). The v0.4 miss SURVIVES the instrument fix — the corrected number is closer to v1's 0.5135 than to v2's 0.6000.
v2 over-reports coverage by ~7 points: its denominator is 30 where the labels say 38. Known direction, recorded as a named limitation.
decisions: v2 lands EXACTLY on the pre-registered floor of 0.6. Reported as the suspicious coincidence it is, not as a pass. A metric arriving precisely at its own bar after being rewritten is the shape score inflation takes.
Not wired in, and the not-wiring is a test rather than a note. Adopting it before blind labels would publish a metric correction as a model improvement.
v0.4 is untouched: it was adjudicated under v1, which is what the shape file registered.

v2's 8 ADDED segments are the open question — mostly symptom and goal claims, and symptoms are not in PROFILE_FIELDS, so they enlarge the denominator with segments no P- id can cover. Logged, not patched.

v2 ADOPTED on the pre-registered comparative criterion. The two miss classes are named limitations, NOT patched: editing the classifier until it stops missing them would fit it to the labels that validated it, and the next definition needs its own blind rating.
Both real miss classes are one mechanism — the subtraction cannot tell asserting POSSESSION of a thing from asserting a clinical PROPERTY of it, and discards the shared term either way.
The 0.6000 coincidence resolves as a coincidence. v2 landing exactly on the old floor was its own denominator being too small, not the model clearing a bar.

okrs.title: A persona cannot claim anything it cannot cite
okrs.desc: Every statement traces to declared state (P/B/J/E) or retrieved graph knowledge — verified by measurement against pre-registered bars, not by inspection.

krs.text: burden & mitigation factual_fraction recover under P/B/J/E while controls (ae, tx, proc) stay flat within 0.10
Inline [F###] markers in raw responses stay at 0 of 30 (v1: 7 of 25)
model_recall above the 0.5 bar on two independent readings

okrs.title: A result reproduces without the author's machine
okrs.desc: Environment declared, locked, verified across every supported interpreter, and stamped into every artifact that claims reproducibility.

krs.text: Full suite green on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 on every push
Every baseline, verdict and bundle stamps python + numpy + lock hash; mismatch refuses
An evidence bundle supports its own reading protocol without external files

okrs.title: Realism comes from data, not from ballparks
okrs.desc: Retire the caveats that currently block quoting the model's own numbers as findings.

krs.text: synthea_loader produces PatientDNA from real Synthea joins (last open build-order item)
A number from cohort/epidemiology.py is quotable as a finding (do-not-quote caveat lifted)
cumulative_burden_weight estimated from a third anchor instead of frozen at zero
